title: Add operator impersonation guard and region-pinned KMS proxy
author: Priya Nair
description:
Context: We observed a class of incidents where long-lived operator tokens and cross-service delegation allowed impersonation of tenant-level operators, bypassing intended RBAC v2 locality checks. Separately, there have been intermittent KMS wrap/unwrap requests routed across regions when downstream callers omitted region pinning headers. This PR introduces two coordinated defenses: 1) an Operator Impersonation Guard in the authz pipeline that detects and blocks suspicious operator-delegation chains (based on token ttl, operator scope changes, and callsite origin validation) and 2) a lightweight Region-Pinned KMS Proxy that enforces KMS region affinity and emits stronger audit hooks for provenance.

Summary of changes: Added authz middleware (authz/impersonation_guard.go) implementing heuristics and configurable thresholds; added RBAC v2 policy hooks and a new operator-claim sanitizer to normalize delegated identities; introduced kms/regio_proxy service with a small proxy layer that validates X-RW-Region headers and rejects or rewrites requests that violate tenant region pins; extended audit pipeline to include a chained-audit-hash (X-RW-Audit-Chain) so downstream services can verify the operator chain and KMS assertion were intact.

Design notes: The impersonation guard is implemented as a non-breaking, opt-in feature behind a feature flag (feature.operator_guard). It evaluates three signals: (a) token age vs requested impersonation ttl, (b) operator scope widening (e.g., service->tenant->org escalation), and (c) callsite origin mismatch (IP/region vs token origin claim). Each signal contributes to a score; when the score exceeds a configurable threshold the request is rejected with 403 and a structured audit event is emitted. The KMS proxy enforces region pinning by checking (in order) tenant metadata, X-RW-Region header, and a fallback operator_region claim. On conflict it rejects with 409 and logs an audit envelope with the signed KMS origin assertion.

Migration and rollout: This change is safe by default. Steps taken: (1) Implemented the guard behind feature.operator_guard=false; (2) added feature flags and config knobs to the console and dedicated configs; (3) added an opt-in canary rollout path in the rollout controller (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automated rollback if audit error rate increases >1.5x; (4) provided an rbac migration script (tools/rbac/migrate_operator_claims_v1_to_v2.sql) to normalize historical operator claims for consistent scoring. Operators should enable the guard in canary, review audit events, and gradually increase rollout.

Testing: Added unit tests for scoring logic (authorization/authz_test.go), integration tests that exercise real KMS with a mocked KMS provider (kms/proxy_integration_test.go), and e2e smoke tests validating that protected routes reject escalated delegation. CI: all checks passed after one flaky storage test rerun.

Security review: Per SEC-119 checklist, we did a threat model pass, validated that no customer key material is materialized by the proxy, and added telemetry hardening to avoid exposing tenant IDs in plain logs. KMS proxy communicates with backends over mTLS; keys remain in the existing KMS envelope flows.

Operational notes: New metrics added (operator_guard.score, operator_guard.block_count, kms_proxy.region_rejects, kms_proxy.audit_chain_verifications) and two alerts: P1 if operator_guard.block_count > 1000/min on main; P2 if kms_proxy.region_rejects spike by 10x in a 5m window. Dashboards updated in observability-pack/security/operator-guard.json.

Related work: Links to Linear tickets ENG-5021 (implement guard), ENG-5074 (kms proxy), SEC-119 (security review).

Merge notes: Squash-merged to main. Post-merge tasks: publish release notes, flip default feature flag to false in dedicated configurations, and coordinate with SRE for canary.

release_notes: Security: Add operator impersonation guard (opt-in) and region-pinned KMS proxy. Adds new audit header X-RW-Audit-Chain (hashed), new metrics, and feature flags for canary rollout. No change to customer-facing API, opt-in only. See docs/security/operator-impersonation-guard.md and docs/kms/region-pinned-proxy.md for configuration.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: false positives could block legitimate delegated workflows (CI, backup agents). Mitigation: service-account whitelist, adjustable scoring thresholds, canary rollout with automated rollback and audit visibility. KMS proxy could surface rejects in cross-region integrations — mitigation: clear 409 error with remediation hints and an operator override gated behind entitlement.
notes_for_ops:
- Enable feature.operator_guard=false by default in production; flip first in staging canary (5%).
- Ensure observability alert rules are imported from observability/dashboards/operator-guard.json.
- If block_count rises unexpectedly, flip feature flag off globally and open ENG-5021 for triage.
